subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: What public Gateway event contract should represent source-run lineage when multiple chat.send requests merge into one executed agent run?
rationale: Current code can identify queued chat turns, but automation should not choose stable API semantics for field naming, ordering, duplicate handling, or whether public runId remains the execution ID.

options.title: Add a lineage array
options.body: Keep runId as the executed/public run ID and add an ordered originalRunIds or sourceRunIds-style field to agent/chat events for merged work.

options.title: Reuse one source ID
options.body: Make merged execution use the first or last queued runId as the public runId, which helps simple clients but loses full lineage.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through accepted responses, session state, and history, accepting that live merged events have no source-run lineage.

recommendation.title: Add a lineage array
recommendation.body: Keep runId as the executed/public run ID and add an ordered originalRunIds or sourceRunIds-style field to agent/chat events for merged work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent-history and timeline signal for Gateway event semantics and queue behavior.
